01

Executive summary

Agent Elite is a product orchestration portal around a real estate website, CRM, marketing and local visibility ecosystem. The accessible system has several distinct application boundaries: a native Home Portal, a white-label iHomefinder CRM, a customized WordPress CMS, and Yext-backed Local Presence. Stripe handles the identifiable billing surface, and Unlayer supplies the observed email designer.

The portal uses Bootstrap 5.1, jQuery and a branded CSS token system behind Kestrel, with Azure App Service DNS routing and Azure AD B2C login. Its exact ASP.NET/.NET runtime and database remain inference or unknown. The CRM exposes React 17 components, Material UI, Redux and a separate JSON API. WordPress reports version 6.8.5 with a Monterey/Genesis theme, custom MU plugins, Gravity Forms, Yoast SEO and Gutenberg. This is a connected collection of native and licensed products, with different identity/role and interface boundaries.

Audit boundary. Existing data, blank forms, menus, settings, public code and sanitized network metadata were inspected. No live customer fields were edited, no form save was submitted, no campaign was sent, no purchase was made, and no permissions were expanded. Ordinary navigation did generate telemetry and automatic provider synchronization requests, including an asset-data PUT and CRM profile-sync POST. Their backend write semantics were not independently established.

Coverage: all seven portal navigation modules; profile, roles, business profiles, activity and billing; CRM leads/tasks/markets/listings/reports; setup secondary pages; campaign designer/automation/texting; WordPress content/forms/widgets/menus; marketplace details for all eleven products; and public IDX/Calendly/UserWay surfaces. “Complete” here means the discovered inventory within this account and audit access, not every plan, hidden staff system or production mutation path.

Principal access limits: Design Studio requires a subscription. Advanced Local Presence launched an external destination but browser inspection was denied at its initial invalid URL; the block was not bypassed. Some delayed report/privacy/MLS screens exposed limited detail. Phone rendering and native mobile-app behavior remain unverified.

What a comparable product must own

Build the account/tenant model, entitlements, CRM records, tasks, routing, campaign policy, reporting definitions, support and provider orchestration. Integrate licensed IDX data, publisher networks, payments, message transport, scheduling and a mature creative editor. Keep provider identities and failure states explicit. Recreating only the dashboard would omit most of the operating system.

Technology stack report

The confidence labels are intentionally categorical. Confirmed is backed by a rendered control, an observed response or an identifiable exposed asset. Supported inference is a reasoned interpretation of clues. Unknown requires access beyond this audit. A loaded dependency is not proof that all its features are used.

Local Presence score implementation

The exposed lp-metrics.js calculates coverage as the proportion of nonduplicate listing rows considered synchronized. Its AI component is the proportion of synchronized rows matching a fixed set of AI/voice publisher identifiers. The headline is a rounded mean of available numeric components, with explicit handling for plan-inapplicable, unavailable and failed data. This is a provider-listing coverage proxy, not a verified result of querying assistants for the business. Exact provider classification and original source metrics still need vendor documentation. Frontend calculation evidence

UI/UX audit and reusable design specification

The portal has a product-centered sidebar, account menu and dashboard cards; account settings place multiple administrative areas in tabs. The CRM uses separate primary and secondary navigation, drawers, dense tables and Material UI dialogs. WordPress keeps its own admin shell and Gutenberg editor. Email design adds another embedded surface. These boundaries are useful to the technical architecture but increase orientation and save-state effort for users.

Prioritized findings

PriorityFindingObserved basisRecommended response
P1 reviewCredential-named URL parametersA WordPress dashboard CRM link contained username/password parameter names with populated values. Values were neither reproduced in artifacts nor used. Their encoding, privilege and lifetime are unknown.
Evidence		Ask the vendor to verify semantics and replace credential-bearing links with expiring one-use handoffs; redact URLs in logs and assess rotation if these are reusable credentials.

P2 reliabilityCustom block compatibilityAn existing landing page displays unsupported awesomeberg/text block notices despite related assets loading.
Evidence		Check block registration/version migration in a sandbox; preserve legacy content and test round-trip edits before changing production.
P2 metric semanticsLocal Presence score/analytics wordingAI Search is a publisher-sync coverage calculation. Profile opens can exceed impressions, yet the UI presents a simplified conversion statement; different cards show 626 and 624 contacts/actions.
Evidence		Publish metric definitions, counts versus unique users, included sources, time windows, denominator, freshness and unavailable states.
P2 commerceCatalog cycle/pricing ambiguityAnnual labels sit beside figures that resemble monthly equivalents; v2 Website detail displayed a particularly large monthly/annual difference. The UI says cycle applies subscription-wide.
Evidence		Show annual invoice total and equivalent monthly rate separately, with taxes/MLS fees and effective date; verify catalog mapping before checkout.
P2 usabilityDense CMS tables at narrow widthLanding-page list columns wrap word by word at the observed narrow viewport. Four UI systems require users to learn different menus and save patterns.
Evidence		Use horizontal scrolling or column priority; provide clear product context, return navigation and consistent saving affordances.
P2 form usabilityPaste suppression defaultGravity Forms custom settings describe disabling paste by default as spam mitigation. No live paste test was performed.
Evidence		Allow paste for ordinary user input; use server validation, rate limits and risk-based spam controls.
P3 polishStale/ambiguous status copyPortal footer says 2025; existing live website says live since just now, and site overview shows the live URL again as staging.
Evidence		Bind lifecycle labels to persisted timestamps and canonical environment URLs; use consistent date/time display.
P3 performance investigationLarge CRM bundle and eager resource loadDownloaded uncompressed main bundle is 10,859,653 bytes; an ordinary reload fetches many CRM datasets. This is not a measured transfer-size or latency benchmark.
Evidence		Measure compressed transfer, main-thread work and route data needs; split heavy editor/chart dependencies and scope fetches by route/permissions.

The CTA color contrast calculation is 2.753:1 using CSS colors, not screenshot pixels. The 13px CTA text is normal-size text, for which the W3C criterion specifies 4.5:1. W3C contrast criterion This is a targeted finding; a complete accessibility conformance audit was not performed. UserWay’s presence does not establish that the website meets a standard.

Responsive evidence and limits

The portal was observed around 894px wide with a hamburger/off-canvas sidebar and around 1036px wide with persistent navigation. The narrow menu opened and closed, and no document overflow was measured on the sampled dashboard. Requested 1440px and 390px overrides did not consistently produce those dimensions; therefore a real phone breakpoint is not claimed as tested. The CMS landing-page table showed heavy word wrapping at narrow width. Touch, zoom, focus trapping, screen-reader and native mobile-app paths remain follow-up tests.

06

Application architecture diagrams

Observed system boundaries

Solid lines represent observed UI/navigation or network relationships, not a packet-level server trace. Dashed lines identify inferred server/API/persistence relationships. A provider box does not imply ownership of the vendor’s backend.

Standalone file: Observed architecture SVG.

Proposed independent system

This design is a recommendation for a new application, not a claim about Agent Elite internals. It keeps native business rules in a modular backend and isolates contracted providers behind adapters and reliable workers.

Standalone file: Proposed architecture SVG.

Data ownership and synchronization

The observed portal has account/member/product data, CRM has lead/team/campaign data, WordPress has content/forms/media, and Local Presence has business-entity/listing data. They should not be treated as a single proven shared database. A rebuild needs durable mappings from tenant/product asset to provider account/entity/site IDs; a change must state its source of truth, synchronization direction, retry policy and last successful reconciliation.

Use a webhook inbox for provider events, an outbox for native changes, stable event/operation IDs and periodic reconciliation. A provider timeout should leave a visible pending/failed job, not silently change local state to success. Do not use browser loads to perform undocumented customer mutations.

Security, operations and maintainability

Check permissions at each API and background-job boundary, not just route visibility. Scope provider mappings and database foreign keys by tenant, including imports, search indexes, media and exports. Require explicit staff access with a reason and audit trail. Keep secrets in a manager and logs free of tokens, contact payloads and sensitive URLs; issue short-lived SSO handoffs. Separate PII/event retention from operational telemetry.

Version schemas, campaign content and metric definitions. Use contract tests against provider sandboxes, deterministic clock tests for workflows, tenant-isolation tests, signed webhook replay tests, content/editor compatibility tests and restore exercises. Deploy stateless web/API containers independently from workers; add indexes and reporting aggregates before adopting a separate warehouse or service split. Choose scale targets and recovery objectives with product requirements rather than inventing them from the GUI.

09

Prioritized rebuild roadmap

This is a sequencing plan, not a fixed cost or date estimate. Staffing, licensed data access, vendor contracts, template scope and migration volume are unknown. Each phase has an acceptance gate that turns architecture into reviewable behavior.

PhaseImplementation scopeReviewable completion evidenceDependency / gate
0. Verification and contractsConfirm product boundaries, provider API/SSO/export rights, feed coverage, required roles, consent model and target scale. Obtain a nonproduction tenant.Approved capability matrix, provider contracts, test fixtures and measurable acceptance criteria.No implementation until the independent scope and integrations are feasible.
1. FoundationTenant/user/role model, OIDC sessions, permission enforcement, product/asset registry, audit trail, migration pipeline, object storage and observability.Cross-tenant negative tests, recovery drill, safe secret handling and local/staging deployment.Tenancy and authorization precede every customer feature.
2. Core CRM and portalDashboard, contact search/import, lead detail, pipeline history, tasks, notes, teams/offices, business profiles, support and billing read views.Deduplicated import preview, accessible table/forms, paginated API and consistent time zone handling.Lead/task/permission acceptance flows pass against sandbox data.
3. Website and IDXManaged CMS or block document system; revisions/templates/media/forms; domains/environments; licensed IDX search/organizer; lead ingestion and routing.Publish/rollback preview, form validation/spam tests, feed freshness checks and routing precedence tests.End-to-end sandbox capture creates exactly one lead with provenance and proper owner.
4. Provider and commerce integrationsStripe checkout/customer flows/reconciliation, Yext profile/listing reporting, calendar, DNS and provisioning adapters.Signed webhook replay/duplicates/out-of-order tests; reconciled entitlements; provider-error and support recovery paths.Customer-visible state stays explainable during provider failure or delayed sync.
5. Automation and marketingVersioned campaign designer, Unlayer templates, trigger rules, scheduling, email/SMS eligibility, greetings, delivery tracking and cancellation/re-enrollment.Clock-controlled tests for delays/time zones; retry idempotency; suppression after opt-out; trigger policy tests.No duplicate sends, no ineligible delivery and no silent scheduled job loss.
6. Advanced products and reportingReview/reputation/social features, creative/print integration, tracked search/AI visibility with honest definitions, comparative reporting and scoped staff admin.Metric reconciliation, provider source/freshness labels, report permissions, media/template compatibility and approval workflows.Claims are backed by measured evidence; premium entitlements are enforced server-side.
7. Production readiness and rolloutCapacity/load tests, dependency review, accessibility audit, backups/restore, alerting, runbooks, staged migration and rollback plan.Canary tenant cohort, delivery/provisioning monitoring, audited migration and ownership for every operational failure mode.Expand only after production reconciliation and recovery evidence is satisfactory.

For the first launch, prioritize a reliable portal, website/IDX capture, native CRM and billing/entitlement reconciliation. Introduce campaign sends only after eligibility, suppression and idempotency are proven. Reputation, print design, social scheduling and real query-based AI visibility should follow measured demand and verified provider access.

Knowledge gaps and verification plan

These are limits of the authorized evidence, not assertions that the capabilities are absent. Paid/staff/nonproduction access and documents can resolve them without bypassing permissions or probing production.

AreaUnverified detailNeeded evidence

Requested viewport overrides did not consistently yield requested dimensions.

Evidence index and reproducibility

The companion structured audit JSON contains the inventory, technology/integration matrices, workflows, findings, proposed entities, stack, roadmap and gaps. Local evidence links point to sanitized screen structures, selected screenshots, network metadata and public assets. The report embeds its screenshots and SVG diagrams, so its main content is portable without a live connection.

The audit is a snapshot dated October 10, 2026 in Asia/Bangkok. Product names, entitlements, pricing, dependencies and external interfaces can change. The report does not certify security, compliance, performance or complete provider implementation. It is an independently prepared functional/technical blueprint, with no source-code replication or application modification.
